summary: Configured Apache on node1 with separate name-based sites on TCP 8080. docs.branch.test and orders.branch.test serve their approved trees; unknown hosts receive HTTP 404. SELinux and firewalld configuration persist. A full node reboot confirmed recovery without changing the OS release, kernel, or staged content.
actions_performed: Installed AlmaLinux-supported Apache and SELinux management utilities.
Configured exact virtual hosts for docs.branch.test and orders.branch.test plus a default 404 catch-all.
Applied persistent httpd_sys_content_t labeling to the staged content.
Enabled Apache and opened TCP 8080 permanently in firewalld.
Verified all supplied files byte-for-byte through their correct virtual hosts.
Safely rebooted node1 and verified its boot identity changed and service behavior recovered.

evidence.requirement: docs.branch.test serves the supplied docs tree on TCP 8080
evidence.summary: Apache's vhost map assigns docs.branch.test to port 8080; index.html and handbook.txt returned HTTP 200 and matched their staged files before and after reboot.

evidence.requirement: orders.branch.test serves the supplied orders tree on TCP 8080
evidence.summary: Apache's vhost map assigns orders.branch.test to port 8080; index.html and catalog.csv returned HTTP 200 and matched their staged files before and after reboot.

evidence.requirement: Unknown Host headers receive an error without tenant content
evidence.summary: Unknown host requests returned HTTP 404 and matched neither tenant's index content, including after reboot.
Individual SHA-256 hashes remained unchanged, and the aggregate content hashset was identical before and after reboot.

evidence.requirement: Configuration is compatible with the existing legacy platform
evidence.summary: Used AlmaLinux repository packages. The system remained AlmaLinux 9.6 with kernel 5.14.0-570.12.1.el9_6 after reboot.

Healthy baseline boot ID 54bd1c3e-3a1b-4913-841b-88512119e096 was captured; safe reboot was acknowledged; the new boot ID was 34b5bae9-21ae-4f3e-af03-59bf23566bab; Apache, listener, firewall, SELinux labels, content, and routing all recovered.
